metadata.metrics_note: Model identity, timing, token and tool-call counts were unavailable. Default metric values are unmeasured placeholders; assertion results and input/output hashes are evidence.

expectations.text: The output treats the installed Sendmux skill and CLI help as the workflow authority instead of fetching and executing runtime instructions.
expectations.evidence: FAIL: 'If its agent supports Skills and the Sendmux pack is missing, install it first' and 'npx skills add Sendmux/skills' mention installing Skills, but do not establish the installed skill and CLI help as workflow authority. No CLI-help direction appears. Absence of runtime fetching does not satisfy the missing authority clause.

expectations.text: The output installs @sendmux/cli when the sendmux binary is unavailable.
expectations.evidence: 'npm install -g @sendmux/cli' appears before registration, providing the installation step in the proposed workflow.

expectations.text: The output runs sendmux agent:register with a profile name and may include --mailbox-local-part, --client-name, --owner-email, or --default.
expectations.evidence: 'sendmux agent:register my-agent' includes '--mailbox-local-part my-agent', '--client-name "My agent"', '--owner-email owner@example.com' and '--default'.

expectations.text: The output says registration does not require an existing account, API key, challenge, or proof of work step.
expectations.evidence: 'No existing account or API key needed' and 'no challenge or proof of work is required.'

expectations.text: The output says the CLI persists the credential securely and does not print it.
expectations.evidence: 'The CLI saves the credential in a permission-restricted profile without printing it'.

expectations.text: The output says the saved profile can read and receive mail without an expiry date while the registration remains active.
expectations.evidence: 'Read and receive mail without an expiry date while registration remains active'.

expectations.text: The output uses sendmux agent:invite-owner when no owner was invited during registration.
expectations.evidence: 'If registration already happened without your email, invite you separately:' followed by 'sendmux agent:invite-owner owner@example.com --profile my-agent --json'.

expectations.text: The output states that storage is capped at 500 MiB before owner approval and raised to at least 5 GiB with sending approval.
expectations.evidence: 'The inbox starts capped at 500 MiB. Owner-approved sending raises it to at least 5 GiB'.

expectations.text: The output says the owner must accept and approve sending before the agent can send.
expectations.evidence: 'Available after you accept the invitation and approve sending.'

expectations.text: The output says Sending CLI commands automatically exchange and cache a one-hour delegated email.send token after approval.
expectations.evidence: 'sending:* commands automatically exchange the saved credential for a one-hour email.send token and cache it until near expiry.'

expectations.text: The output says a full registration revoke removes read access and delegated sending access.
expectations.evidence: 'A full registration revoke removes read access, the owner link, invitation/recovery handles and all derived sending tokens.'

expectations.text: The output treats the installed Sendmux skill and CLI help as the workflow authority instead of fetching and executing runtime instructions.
expectations.evidence: response.md: "Use the Sendmux getting-started skill and the installed CLI’s `--help` as the setup authority." The answer supplies local CLI commands and does not instruct fetching or executing runtime instructions.

expectations.text: The output installs @sendmux/cli when the sendmux binary is unavailable.
expectations.evidence: response.md gives the installation command before registration: "npm install -g @sendmux/cli". This is a planning answer; its final note explicitly says "Not run: installation, registration, connection checks or invitations."

expectations.text: The output runs sendmux agent:register with a profile name and may include --mailbox-local-part, --client-name, --owner-email, or --default.
expectations.evidence: response.md includes "sendmux agent:register my-agent" with "--mailbox-local-part my-agent", "--client-name "My agent"", "--owner-email owner@example.com", "--default" and "--json".

expectations.text: The output says registration does not require an existing account, API key, challenge, or proof of work step.
expectations.evidence: response.md: "Your agent can register a new Sendmux inbox without an existing account or API key." Also: "No challenge or proof of work is required."

expectations.text: The output says the CLI persists the credential securely and does not print it.
expectations.evidence: response.md: "The CLI saves registration state, stores the credential in a permission-restricted local profile without printing it, and waits up to 10 minutes for mailbox readiness."

expectations.text: The output says the saved profile can read and receive mail without an expiry date while the registration remains active.
expectations.evidence: response.md, Saved agent profile row: "Read and receive email without an expiry date while registration remains active."

expectations.text: The output uses sendmux agent:invite-owner when no owner was invited during registration.
expectations.evidence: response.md: "If registration already happened without `--owner-email`, invite yourself separately:" followed by "sendmux agent:invite-owner owner@example.com --profile my-agent --json".

expectations.text: The output states that storage is capped at 500 MiB before owner approval and raised to at least 5 GiB with sending approval.
expectations.evidence: response.md: "The inbox starts with a 500 MiB cap; owner-approved sending raises it to at least 5 GiB."

expectations.text: The output says the owner must accept and approve sending before the agent can send.
expectations.evidence: response.md, Delegated Sending token row: "Available only after you accept the invitation and approve sending." The final line also says "Sending remains unavailable until your approval."

expectations.text: The output says Sending CLI commands automatically exchange and cache a one-hour delegated email.send token after approval.
expectations.evidence: response.md: "`sending:*` commands then automatically exchange the durable credential for a one-hour `email.send` token and cache it until near expiry." This follows "Available only after you accept the invitation and approve sending."

expectations.text: The output says a full registration revoke removes read access and delegated sending access.
expectations.evidence: response.md: "Revoking the full registration removes read access, the owner link, invitation/recovery handles and all derived sending tokens."
